prompt: What made it possible, by 2020, for Vite to stop bundling during development?
hint: What browsers had learnt to do on their own.

choices.text: Webpack had become fast enough to bundle on every save
choices.why: Vite did not make the bundling faster; it took the bundling out of development.

choices.text: Every browser in use loaded ES modules natively
choices.why: Right. With `<script type="module">` and `import` everywhere, each file could be served as its own module.

choices.text: Rust made bundling the whole app take no time
choices.why: Rolldown is written in Rust and does the build, but the dev server still serves your files one by one.

choices.text: Vue 3 no longer needed `.vue` files converted
choices.why: `.vue` files are still converted, by `@vitejs/plugin-vue`, as each one is asked for.

prompt: Which of these build on Vite, as the lesson describes them? Choose all that apply.
hint: One of the wrong ones is the tool Vite replaced.

choices.text: Nuxt
choices.why: Right. Nuxt is built on Vite; lesson 18 uses it.

choices.text: Vue CLI
choices.why: Vue CLI ran webpack. It is what Vite replaced, and it is in maintenance now.

choices.text: Vitest
choices.why: Right. The lesson calls it Vite running tests.

choices.text: The Angular CLI's development server
choices.why: Right. It has used Vite since Angular 17.

choices.text: webpack
choices.why: webpack is the bundler Vue CLI ran, a different tool from Vite and from Rolldown.

prompt: How many requests did the week page make to the dev server?
hint: The count `grep -c` printed.

prompt: `curl` of `/src/planner.ts` from the dev server printed `isoDate(date)` with no `: Date`. What checked the types on the way?
hint: Which script exists apart from `dev`, and why?

choices.text: `@vitejs/plugin-vue`, as it converted the file
choices.why: That plugin converts `.vue` files, and `planner.ts` is not one; it does not check types either.

choices.text: The browser, as it loaded the TypeScript
choices.why: The browser never sees TypeScript: what arrives is JavaScript.

choices.text: The dev server, which refuses a file with a type error
choices.why: It refuses nothing on types; a type error is stripped and served like the rest.

choices.text: Nothing; checking is left to `vue-tsc`
choices.why: Right. Stripping takes a moment per file, checking takes seconds for the project, so `type-check` runs apart.

prompt: Why does the dev server rewrite `from 'vue'` in `main.ts` to an address under `/node_modules/.vite/deps/`?
hint: Think of what the browser would do with the word `vue` alone.

choices.text: A browser has no idea where a bare name like `vue` lives
choices.why: Right. The browser loads addresses, so the server swaps each bare name for one it serves.

choices.text: To check the installed Vue against `package.json`
choices.why: Nothing compares versions there; the `?v=` part changes with the dependencies so the cache stays right.

choices.text: Because a file was renamed to `.ts` in lesson 16
choices.why: That was `router.js`, a file of yours, and it became `/src/router.ts`. `vue` is a package.

choices.text: So the browser fetches Vue from a CDN
choices.why: The address is on the dev server itself, a folder inside your project.

prompt: The page is on the week of 26 October after a click on *Next week*. You change only the `<h1>` in `HomeView.vue`'s template and save. What does the page show?
hint: What a template change replaces, and what it leaves alone.

choices.text: The old heading until you reload by hand
choices.why: The update was hot: the page logged `hot updated`, and the new heading was there.

choices.text: A full reload of the page, landing on the current week
choices.why: A `.vue` file accepts its own updates, so nothing had to reload.

choices.text: The new heading, back on the week of 19 October
choices.why: That is what a change to `<script setup>` did, because setup ran again.

choices.text: The new heading, still on the week of 26 October
choices.why: Right. Only the render function is replaced; the instance and its `monday` ref stay.

prompt: The edit to `HomeView.vue`'s `<script setup>` was only a comment, and the page still went back to the week of 19 October. Why?
hint: Vite does not read what the new script means.

choices.text: The comment broke the `monday` ref, and Vue fell back to a default
choices.why: The comment changed no code. The state was rebuilt because setup ran again, not because anything broke.

choices.text: Setup runs again, since Vite cannot know the state would match
choices.why: Right. The component is created anew, and `monday` comes from `weekStart(new Date())`.

choices.text: The store reset the week when it reloaded its sessions
choices.why: The store lives in its own module and kept its sessions; the week is the component's `monday` ref.

choices.text: A comment counts as a template change
choices.why: A template change kept the 26th in the first capture; this edit was in the script.

prompt: An edit to `planner.ts` reloaded the whole page, though `HomeView` imports it and would take the update. Why?
hint: Follow every importer, not only the one on screen.

choices.text: Plain `.ts` files are left out of HMR
choices.why: They are in it: the update goes up through their importers until one accepts it.

choices.text: `HomeView` refused it because the week had changed
choices.why: A `.vue` file accepts its own updates; the refusal was at the top of another path.

choices.text: A path through the store and the router reaches `main.ts`, which nobody imports
choices.why: Right. On that path the update reaches the top with nobody to take it, and a full reload is all that is left.

choices.text: A change to a TypeScript file forces a full reload, so that the types are checked first
choices.why: The dev server checks no types; the edit was a comment, and it would have been stripped like any type.

prompt: How many files did `vite build` list in its output, `dist/index.html` included?
hint: One `dist/` line per file.

prompt: Why may a server tell browsers to keep the files in `dist/assets` for a year?
hint: Look at their names.

choices.text: Vite builds them once and later builds leave them alone
choices.why: Each build writes them again, and a code change gives them new contents; the cache is safe because the names change too.

choices.text: `index.html` carries a version the browser compares
choices.why: `index.html` has no version; it names the hashed files, and it is the one file whose name stays the same.

choices.text: A hash of the contents is in each name
choices.why: Right. Changed code arrives under a new name, which `index.html` points to.

choices.text: Vite compresses them for caching, as it does `public/`
choices.why: `public/` is copied as it is, never processed; the size of a file has nothing to do with how long it is cached.

prompt: Under `vite preview` the week page made four requests, where the dev server needed 33. What accounts for the difference?
hint: What the build did with the modules.

choices.text: The preview kept the other 29 in the browser's cache
choices.why: Those 29 files do not exist in `dist`: there is nothing separate to cache.

choices.text: HMR sends the rest over its WebSocket
choices.why: A build has no HMR client, which is why no `[vite] connecting...` appeared.

choices.text: The build joined the modules into few files
choices.why: Right. The page, the stylesheet, the script and the data: four.

choices.text: The preview skips the components the week page does not show
choices.why: Only the lazy course routes were split off; the week page's components are inside `index`.

prompt: The planner's `dist` is on a host. A link to `/courses/spanish` works when clicked inside the planner, and gives a 404 when the address is typed. What is missing?
hint: What did `vite preview` answer for that address, and with which file?

choices.text: A file called `courses/spanish` in `dist`
choices.why: There is no such file even under `vite preview`, which answered 200; the router draws the page.

choices.text: A route for `/courses/spanish` in `vite.config.js`
choices.why: Routes live in the router; the configuration lists no pages.

choices.text: The dev server's HMR client, which the build leaves out
choices.why: The click works without it, and so would the typed address once the host answers.

choices.text: The host serving `index.html` where no file exists
choices.why: Right. `createWebHistory` needs it; that is the redirects of `front-delivery` lesson 4.

prompt: With `server: { port: 5173, strictPort: true }`, what happens when a second dev server starts while the first is running?
hint: `strictPort` is what lesson 1 did not have.

choices.text: It takes 5174 and says so
choices.why: That is the default without `strictPort`, and the tab on 5173 keeps talking to the first server.

choices.text: It waits until 5173 is free, then starts
choices.why: It does not wait: it stops with an error at once.

choices.text: It stops with `Port 5173 is already in use`
choices.why: Right. An error that stops you beats a server on a port you are not looking at.

choices.text: It takes over 5173 and the first server stops
choices.why: Two servers do not share a port, and the first one keeps running.

prompt: Where and when does `vite.config.js` run?
hint: It may import packages and read files.

choices.text: In the browser, before the page's first module
choices.why: A browser could not read files from your disk; the configuration is for Vite, not for the page.

choices.text: Inside `vue-tsc`, while it checks types
choices.why: `vue-tsc` checks the code; it is not what reads the configuration.

choices.text: Inside the bundle, as a module of the app
choices.why: Nothing of it reaches `dist`; it decides how `dist` is made.

choices.text: In Node, before the server starts or the build begins
choices.why: Right. That is why it imports packages and computes values freely.

prompt: A project uses `server.proxy` so that `/api` reaches a backend on port 3000. Once the build is deployed, what passes `/api` on to the backend?
hint: Which of Vite's servers are there in production?

choices.text: The host, or whatever sits in front of the backend
choices.why: Right. A build is a folder of files; the proxy belongs to Vite's two servers.

choices.text: The proxy, which the build writes into `index.html`
choices.why: `index.html` names the script and the stylesheet and nothing else.

choices.text: `vite preview`, which serves the built folder to students
choices.why: `vite preview` is for looking at a build on your computer, not for serving students.

choices.text: The browser, which reads `server.proxy` from the configuration
choices.why: The configuration runs in Node before the server or the build; no browser reads it.

prompt: `.env` holds `VITE_DATA_URL=/courses.json` and `PLANNER_NOTE=not-for-the-browser`. After a build, which values are in the bundle?
hint: Count what the two `grep`s found.

choices.text: Both, since the store could read either
choices.why: The note was in the bundle nowhere: Vite exposes only the names that start with `VITE_`.

choices.text: Neither; they are looked up when the page runs
choices.why: Vite replaces the expression with its value as it builds, and `courses.json` was found once.

choices.text: Only `PLANNER_NOTE`, since build settings are unprefixed
choices.why: It is the other way round: the unprefixed note stays out of the bundle.

choices.text: Only `/courses.json`
choices.why: Right. The prefix decides, and the value is written into the file.

prompt: `VITE_DATA_URL` is `/courses.json` in `.env` and `/staging.json` in `.env.staging`, and the shell that runs `vite build --mode staging` has `VITE_DATA_URL=/test.json` set. Which address ends up in the bundle?
hint: The order runs from weakest to strongest, and there is a fifth place after the four files.

choices.text: `/staging.json`
choices.why: The mode's file beats `.env`, but a variable already set in the shell beats both.

choices.text: `/test.json`
choices.why: Right. A variable set in the shell that started Vite beats all four files.

choices.text: `/courses.json`
choices.why: `.env` is the weakest of the files and loses to both others here.

choices.text: None: the build stops on the conflict
choices.why: Three values for one name is no conflict; the strongest wins.

prompt: Without `strictImportMetaEnv`, a name on `import.meta.env` that `env.d.ts` never declared is accepted and typed as ___.
hint: The TypeScript type that accepts anything.

prompt: The dev server is running when somebody changes a session in `courses.json` to the course `piano`. What does `check-planner-data` say, and when?
hint: When does `buildStart` run?

choices.text: An error in the browser on the next save
choices.why: `buildStart` runs once when the server starts; a save does not call it.

choices.text: An error at once in the dev server's terminal
choices.why: That would need a file watcher, through `configureServer`; this plugin has only `buildStart`.

choices.text: Nothing, until the next start or the next build
choices.why: Right. The build always runs the check, and the build is what reaches students.

choices.text: A warning the next time the week page loads
choices.why: The plugin runs in Vite, not in the page; the page would show the id and say nothing.

prompt: The hook that receives the code of every file before it is served, and may change it, is `___`. It is how `plugin-vue` turns a `.vue` file into JavaScript.
hint: Not `load`, which invents a module.

prompt: Why is `checkPlannerData` a function that returns the plugin object, rather than the object itself?
hint: `vue()` is written the same way.

choices.text: Vite calls the function again before each hook
choices.why: The configuration calls it once, in `plugins: [vue(), checkPlannerData()]`, and Vite gets the object.

choices.text: It is the convention every plugin follows, so options have somewhere to go
choices.why: Right. This plugin takes none yet, and `vue()` is the same shape.

choices.text: `this.error` works only inside a returned object
choices.why: `this` is the context Vite passes to the hook; it has nothing to do with the function around it.

choices.text: So the plugin is left out of the bundle
choices.why: The plugin runs in Node with the configuration and never reaches the bundle, function or not.

prompt: Put what `npm run build` did, in the planner, in the order it happened.
hint: The script has two commands, and a plugin's `buildStart` runs before any file is processed.
items: The chunks are rendered and their gzip sizes computed
Vite lists the files in `dist` with their sizes

prompt: Match each file edited and saved while the dev server runs to what the lesson shows happening.
hint: Three of them are in the section on HMR, one in the section on the configuration.

pairs.right: the component updates and keeps its state

pairs.left: a comment at the top of `planner.ts`

pairs.right: the server restarts on its own

right_distractors: the whole application is bundled again

prompt: A teammate puts `VITE_ADMIN_PASSWORD=…` in `.env.local`, reasoning that `.local` files stay out of git, so the password stays private. What is wrong with that?
hint: Two separate rules: one about git, one about the prefix.

choices.text: `create-vue`'s `.gitignore` leaves `.local` files in
choices.why: It has a line `*.local`, so git does leave the file out. The leak is elsewhere.

choices.text: `.env.local` is read in development alone, so the build fails
choices.why: It is read in every mode; `.env.[mode].local` is the one that belongs to a mode.

choices.text: Nothing; a value in a `.local` file stays on one computer
choices.why: The file stays on one computer, and its `VITE_` value is written into the built JavaScript.

choices.text: The prefix puts the value in the bundle every visitor downloads
choices.why: Right. The prefix is a promise that the value is fit to publish; a secret stays on a server.

prompt: Which of these hold for the dev server and not for a build served by `vite preview`? Choose all that apply.
hint: Compare the two `look` captures and the footer.

choices.text: Each module the page imports is a request of its own
choices.why: Right. Thirty-three requests against four.

choices.text: TypeScript types are stripped from the code sent
choices.why: Both send JavaScript with no types; the build runs `vue-tsc` first and still strips them.

choices.text: The page opens a WebSocket for updates
choices.why: Right. A build has no HMR client, so the preview printed no `[vite] connecting...`.

choices.text: `import.meta.env.MODE` is `development`
choices.why: Right. The preview's footer said `production build`.

choices.text: `/courses/spanish` is answered with `index.html`
choices.why: The lesson shows `vite preview` doing exactly that, with a 200.
